name: Split squat / lunge
angleNote: Front-knee flexion: 40° = top, 100° = bottom. Lifting makes the angle smaller. Torques are for the front leg.

strength.note: Relative hip-extension torque vs hip flexion, assumed strongest with the hip bent. Peak is per leg, typical trained adult. Approximate.
strength.source: TODO: verify against published torque–angle data

strength.note: Relative knee-extension torque vs knee flexion, weakest near straight, strongest around 60°. Peak is per leg. Approximate.
strength.source: TODO: verify against published torque–angle data

strength.note: Relative plantarflexion torque, strongest with the calf stretched. Peak is per leg. Approximate.
strength.source: TODO: verify against published torque–angle data

muscles.name: Quadriceps
muscles.note: Knee extensors: their share follows the knee torque.

muscles.name: Adductor magnus
muscles.note: Rear part extends the hip, more so when it is deeply bent.

muscles.name: Calves (soleus, gastrocnemius)
muscles.note: Plantarflexors: keep the shin from tipping forward.

phases.name: Mid-range
phases.text: Lowering: how the weight splits between the legs depends on where the centre of mass is.

phases.name: Bottom
phases.text: Deepest point: largest front-knee and hip torques.

variants.name: Bulgarian split squat (dumbbells)
variants.equipment: Dumbbells, rear foot on a bench
variants.notes: Rear foot on a bench behind you, trunk nearly upright. Most of the weight is on the front leg.

variants.name: Bulgarian split squat, forward lean
variants.equipment: Dumbbells, rear foot on a bench
variants.notes: Leaning the trunk forward and keeping the shin more vertical moves torque from the knee to the hip, and shifts the weight further onto the front leg.

variants.name: Split squat / static lunge (barbell)
variants.equipment: Barbell, rear foot on the floor
variants.notes: Rear foot on the floor, up on its toes. The rear leg takes a bigger share than in the Bulgarian version.
